headline: A Funny Farce:' Loot,' Based on a Play, Opens at Baronet
abstract: The plot of "Loot," the film version of the late Joe Orton's second play, a very bitter, very funny farce, should be got out of the way as quickly and as sanely as possible:What the undertaker tactfully refers to as Mr. McLeavy's "first bereavement" is Mrs. McLeavy, whose newly embalmed body, dressed in her beloved Woman's Army Service uniform with sensible shoes to match, lies in a coffin in the parlor of Mr. McLeavy's seedy hotel, located in the suburbs of what seems to be an especially ghastly English provincial city.Upstairs Mrs. McLeavy's nurse, Fay, who looks like a marvelous, life-sized Kewpie doll and who walks like the sort of French maid you might describe as saucy, is trying to persuade Mr. McLeavy to become her eighth husband.Downstairs Mrs. McLeavy's son, Hal, who hasn't quite cleared the homosexual hurdle, and his best friend, Dennis, who has, are trying to hide the loot from their bank robbery in Mum's coffin, which means stuffing Mum into the dumbwaiter, upside down. Meanwhile, the premises are crawling with a crooked policeman, Mr. Truscott ("You surround the property," he says to his men. "I'll surround the house"), disguised as a member of the Metropolitan Water Board.Everything goes so systematically wrong that there has to be a happy ending for just about everybody but Mr. McLeavy, the very dumb, Roman Catholic innocent who may, just possibly, be the only character in the script with whom Mr. Orton was unsympathetic. "I've raised a ghoul at my own expense!" he cries when he learns Hal has been tampering with Mum's corpse.At another point, the mourning husband demands to be able to open his wife's coffin. "She's my wife. I can do what I like with her." Says the shocked policeman, who is about to divide the bank loot with Hal, Dennis and Fay: "Indeed not, sir. Conjugal rights should stop with the last heart beat!"I quote this dialogue at some length because there are still enough examples of Mr. Orton's displacements of conventional attitudes to make the movie "Loot" quite funny. However, Silvio Narizzano, the director, in making a movie out of the one-set play has not simply opened it up, he has also put it on the rack.He has stretched it out with no great imagination, not only by showing us all of the action that takes place outside the hotel, but by making a movie, that is, by cross-cutting between scenes of simultaneous action and by breaking up individual scenes into close-ups, medium shots and long shots. The effect, which is as deadening to Orton as to Feydeau, is one of constant, nearly fatal interruption.This sort of thing puts a very real strain on the performers, who are being rediscovered with each shot, even if they haven't actually been off-stage. In spite of these handicaps, I liked them all, including Lee Remick as the nurse whose Irish brogue tends to come and go according to the length of any speech; Richard Attenborough as the policeman who often sounds like Margaret Rutherford; Roy Holder as the androgynous son who looks like Rita Tushingham; Hywell Bennett as Dennis, and especially Milo O'Shea as poor old Mr. McLeavy.However, while watching "Loot," which opened yesterday at the Baronet, one is likely to mistake Mr. Orton's contempt for church, state, the judiciary, the police, and heaven knows what else for the second rate satirist's contempt for feeling. The good satirist wears his heart not on his sleeve, nor any other place else so obvious, but in his style.

headline: '4 Flies on Grey Velvet,' Suspense Film
abstract: "Four Flies on Grey Velvet," is the third suspense thriller from Italy's Dario Argento. It has striking, imaginative color photography and deep-freeze pacing and atmosphere. But they're simply not enough, even in such a classy, handsome production.The plot and dénouement are not only old but farfetched, and the dialogue is banal. The characters are generally a flabby lot, ranging from young urban jet-setters to scruffy bohemians.Nor are the performances of Michael Brandon, as the jittery, badgered hero, and Mimsy Farmer, as his wife, especially compelling, though Miss Farmer does handle one scene brilliantly. Mr. Argento injects some sourly wry humor with the appearance of a fluttery private detective, an admitted homosexual and sleuthing flop, played by Jean Pierre Marielle. The nearest thing to sensibility and balance is a raffish sage alertly underplayed by Bus Spencer. And Francine Racette, as the hero's pretty mistress, does well in one scene of whimpering terror.A spine-tingling sequence of a doomed, blackmailing servant trapped in a park at dusk is superb and typifies Mr. Argento at his chilling best.In the guesswork department, Mr. Argento and his two writer colleagues simply aren't fair. All that circuitous teasing and those red herrings don't produce a shred of real evidence to nibble on. You're on your own, in pure hit-or-miss speculation.Furthermore, except for one brief segment cueing in the title (a "scientific" conjecture nobody will swallow), where on earth are the police? With four murders clearly leading to the hero's doorstep, his unguarded attractive residence (apparently in midtown) should be blazing with lights. Instead, Mr. Argento seals it off, in shadows and eerie sounds, like a Wuthering Heights.But you'll hang on, we guarantee, to see and hear the culprit at the end. There, emphatically, M. Agento has us.

abstract: Corp Counsel's office chief of penalities div I Rubin repts on Nov 29 that new procedure to covercome const objections to seizure of allegedly pornographic material has been devised by NYC law enforcement agencies; says that under new approach plainclothesmen from Police Dept's public morals squad will not attempt to seize on the spot pornographic materials they had seen; policemen will 1st prepare affidavit describing material and submit it to Criminal Ct judge; if judge agrees that material justifies seizures for alleged obscenity, he issues warrant to that effect; policemen then return with warrant to make arrests and seizures; approach is designed to eliminate objections raised by Criminal Ct Judge H J Rothwax, who 2 wks ago threw out 135 cases involving seizure of peepshow films and literature by police who had deemed material obscene; Rothwax ruled that police 'cannot be properly entrusted with the task of determining what is obscene'; morals squad, acting under existing procedure, repts it raided bookstore, Bob's Bargain, seizing 21 peepshow machines and arresting mgr K Cunningham on charges of promoting obscenity; premises was identified as belonging to E R Finch

headline: The Screen:Museum Opens 'Here Comes Every Body'
abstract: The group encounter documentary called "Here Comes Every Body" is by far the most interesting feature of this kind I have seen. Some of these soul-baring talk sessions on film have been candid, crashing bores, in the name of truth and cinéma vérité (alert the camera and shoot). As the first movie of an English director-producer, John Whitmore, the California-made project does credit to him and to the Whitney Museum, which unveiled the film yesterday for a seven-day run.For one thing, these people have something to say about themselves and one another. They are generally personable and intelligent. Their revelations and confessed hang-ups are tactfully prodded by a wise group director as they gather in a room and relax on the pool terrace of the Esalen Institute in Big Sur. Finally, as Mr. Whitmore's unobtrusive camera concentrates on seven or eight case histories—out of 16 participants—they seem people worth knowing. Their tears, when they flow, matter. So do the exploding tensions and fears. Finally, they speak plain English, with explicit, obscene shortcuts.The one we especially liked was a fading, 44-year-old woman — warm-hearted, fat—who yearns for children, we learn, and "was once young and beautiful." In the most touching moment she wails, "Where has it all gone?"One genial young man, a frank homosexual, berates his hypersensitivity with a directness that is downright manly. An older, baldish man learns to cushion his strikeout hostility. Of the troubled couples, two attractive youngsters are as winning as they are candid.The whole thing leaves a frank, stimulating taste. An open-minded viewer — and listener—should come to care for the participants even as they learn to care for one another.

headline: NEW JERSEY
abstract: New Brunswick HS (NJ) is closed on Dec 18 as result of protest by 300 black students over suspension of black English teacher, W Dunbar; on Dec 17, New Brunswick Educ Bd met and voted suspension pending disposition of charges brought against Dunbar, who was arrested on Dec 17, along with D Harris, in men's room of Penn Central rr station and charged with committing indecent act in public place and with trespassing on rr property; Educ Bd meets on Dec 18 in secret location to decide whether to reopen school on Dec 19

headline: 4 More Inmates Are Named in Attica Indictments
abstract: 4 more Attica prison inmates are charged on Dec 20 with kidnapping, sodomy, assault and robbery in connection with Sept, '71 prison uprising; J Richey, who receives 1 of largest indictments so far, is accused of 37 counts of kidnapping for his alleged role in rounding up 8 hostages and threatening them with execution; 34 men have been accused already in 27 sealed indictments; 10 indictments remain to be opened; R Jackson is accused of stealing prison key; G Felder is charged with kidnapping and assaulting 3 hostages and R Wright with committing sodomy with fellow inmate; speculation runs rampant on whether state troopers or prison guards will be indicted

headline: LBJ Park Expansion Is Planned, But Some Landowners Resist
abstract: Texas Parks and Wildlife Comm has decided to expand Lyndon B Johnson State Park with $1-million voted by state Legis in 1971, from its present 269 acres to total of 819 acres; plans revive decision in 1966, abandoned because of money shortage and property owner interests, to enlarge park; decision to enlarge park amends 1966 action to include land on river across the Pedernales from river frontage Johnsons are donating to Govt; 6 landowners are involved in decision; they are hesitant about allowing properties to be condemned since this would mean that lawyers would share proceeds

headline: Poland Seeks to Listen to Public Opinion
abstract: Increased debate of crucial issues, demanded by Polish party leader Gierek in effort to prevent repetition of conditions that brought Poland to 'brink of civil war' in '70, discussed; S Celichowski, editor of Gdansk party newspaper Glos Wybrzerza, notes discussion is 'the vogue now' but indicates it is not enough, int; notes information from top down is easy, but from bottom up it is still heavily filtered; says under consultation system introduced by Gierek draft proposals of all econ changes are sent to nation's 100 largest enterprises, where they are discussed with workers in mass meetings or with workers' reprs; asserts consultations work well between party activists but degenerate into arguments when workers are finally involved; describes as an example the effort to formulate natl labor code

headline: Homosexual Wins Fight to Take Bar Examination in Minnesota
abstract: Minnesota bar examiners rule J Baker, outspoken leader of Gay Liberation Movement, is eligible for state bar exams since he did not fraudently obtain license with which he entered into homosexual marriage with J M McConnel in Sept '71; Minn State Bd of Law Examiners had invited him to hearing to answer questions about his application for marriage license in Mankato, Minn; at issue was state law that requires candidates for bar and other professions to be of 'good moral character' not Baker's avowed homosexuality; procedures through which license was obtained detailed

headline: An American Family Lives Its Life on TV
abstract: American Family, An: S Harrington revs An American Family, TV documentary that chronicles life and problems of W C Loud family of Santa Barbara, Calif; family consists of husband Bill, wife Pat and 5 children; parents' refusal to acknowledge that their oldest son is homosexual is one problem that confronts family; program was produced by C Gilbert and presented on WNET; family illus

headline: Parents Go to Albany to Ask Day‐Care Fee Freeze
abstract: Hundreds of NYS parents and soc workers on Jan 8 lobby in Albany to confront NYS Soc Services Comr A Lavine on issue of increased day-care fees; basic grievance is that low-paid 'working poor' cannot afford higher fees ordered by NYS and will have to go back on welfare; Lavine reiterates past announcements that state will supply $15-million in extra aid to city to permit those families in present city program to continue with current fees for next 18 mos, while rest of state's non-welfare families pay higher fees; also promises to meet with leaders of Ad Hoc Com to Save Our Children to try to work out compromise; NYC Day Care Council exec dir M Grosett says temporary aid has 'invidious' side to it because it means dual standard whereby newly applying working poor families will have to pay higher fees than families already in program; Lavine promises to meet with NYC Soc Services Comr Sugarman, who is in attendance, to see whether dual standard can be avoided; illus

headline: Court Refuses Admission to Bar Because of a 1955 Homosexual Arrest
abstract: NYS Appellate Div on Jan 8 denies admission to NYS bar to H L Kimball, 47-yr-old homosexual who in '55 was arrested in Fla on sodomy charge and disbarred; majority opinion of 3-2 decision was written by Justice J D Hopkins; it contends that act for which Kimball was arrested in '55 was at that time a felony in NY and had his arrest taken place in NY Kimball would have been disbarred immediately; Hopkins says NYS law makes 'deviate sexual intercourse' a misdemeanor and that Justices H J Latham and F J Munder, who concurred in decision, back his view that it militates against eligibility of an applicant to bar; Justices M H Martuscello and J I Shapiro sharply counter position; NY CLU criticizes majority opinion; Kimball comments

headline: Court, Overruling State, Gives Gay Alliance Right to Incorporate
abstract: NYS Appeals Ct, 6-0, reaffirms on Jan 12 right of group of homosexuals known as Gay Activist Alliance to receive certificate of incorporation under that name; declares that Sec of State Lomenzo had acted arbitrarily when he denied group's petition to incorporate; asserts that Lomenzo lacked authority to label alliance's purposes violative of public policy; alliance spokesman says group will benefit from incorporation by having legal protection as individuals for its officers and members; alliance originally appealed decision by Sup Ct Justice Kane, who in '71 upheld Lomenzo's ruling

headline: Phase 3 or Phaseout?
abstract: ed on Nixon's Phase 3 econ stabilization program holds Adm runs serious risk in loosening controls with inflationary pressures still so strong and econ still so far from full employment; says pol logic behind limited mandatory controls appears to be that Nixon is eager to consolidate his new alliance with organized labor and to give his business supporters respite from profit margin limits; expresses 'gravest doubts' that 'stick in the closet' approach to disciplining business and labor will work; holds Adm must defend its standards with vigilance and skill or Phase 3 will degenerate into Phase 0 or force return to all-out controls

headline: Making War, Not Love
abstract: T Wicker article comments on Pres war powers in light of Nixon's ordering of Christmas bombing campaign against N Vietnam; says Adm sources admitted bombing was intended to show Hanoi 'the extent of his anger over what he regards as an eleventh-hr reneging on peace terms' and also to force Hanoi to 'negotiate seriously'; asks if a Pres could, on future occasions, order similar bombings for diplomatic reasons; says problem is to retain Presidents's capacity to function as Comdr in Chief, but to define or restrain that function so that he cannot order acts of war by 'whim, impulse, tantrum or imperial decision'; notes Sen Goldwater's criticism of moves to restrict Pres war powers by 'members of a pol party whose leaders got us into this war' and Prof A Schlesinger Jr article on Pres war powers

headline: Gay Alliance Seeks to Revive Rights Bill in Council
abstract: 8 members of NYC City Council com--a majority--on Jan 14 sign Gay Activist Alliance petition for reconsidering twice defeated bill that would bar discrimination against homosexuals in employment and housing; NYC City Council Majority Leader T J Cuite refuses to recognize petition as proper legis procedure; notes that neither Gen Welfare Com chmn Councilman S S Sharison nor other members have pressed for another meeting on bill; asserts bill will remain in Gen Welfare Com, but meeting specifically to reconsider it must be scheduled; 2 of 8 members who signed petition indicate that they will vote against bill at full Council meeting; say they feel bill should be voted out of com so that matter can be dealt with by entire council

headline: Metropolitan Briefs
abstract: Three similar murders in three weeks in Greenwich Village involving men who might have been part of the “leather bar” scene have sent waves of rumors and fear through the area's homosexual community.

headline: Homosexuals in ‘Village’ Fearful After Series of Similar Killings
abstract: 3 similarly violent murders in 3 wks in Lower Manhattan involving men described by police as being part of homosexual scene have sent waves of rumor and fear throughout area's homosexual community; leaders of Gay Activist Alliance have called for more police protection following discovery of murders, in which all three victims were stabbed numerous times and found in apts apparently deliberately set on fire; 1st victim was R Cabo, found on Jan 4; others victims, identified as D MacNiven and J P W Beardsley were found on Jan 8; body of student R Borrero, found in Hudson River near Morton St pier in Greenwich Village, is not linked to others

headline: RIVER DEATHS RAISE HOMOSEXUALS' FEAR
abstract: discovery on Jan 17 of 2 bodies in Hudson River off Greenwich Village adds to fears of homosexual community, already stunned by 3 murders of homosexuals in area; police, declining to link recent murders to others, identify 1 of bodies as R Borrero

headline: LAZAR FORESEES IMPROVED TAXIS
abstract: NYC Taxi Comm Chmn Lazar says taxicabs will be safer and more comfortable within next 2 mos and that '73 could bring 'an end to the gypsy-cab problem,' int with NY Times eds and reporters; says about 5,000 livery license plates, used by most operators of so-called gypsy cabs, were not renewed in '73; discloses that additional 1,000 nonmedallion cabs have been licensed by city as 'limousines,' with 3,000 additional applications for limousine licenses pending; says limousine license plate entitles its holder to carry passenger for hire but not to answer hails from st; A Andrews, Bklyn atty who represents nonmedallion drivers, agrees that number of gypsy drivers probably has dwindled but doubts that non-renewal figure was 5,000; accuses police and comm inspectors of 'entrapment and harassment' in their attempt to drive nonmedallion drivers off sts; Lazar insists that comm inspectors only go after flagrant violators of law against cruising by nonmedallion cabs; is 'much heartened' by stepped-up police action against gypsy operators; reveals that 1,000 Chevrolet taxis have been banned because they do not meet comm specifications; contends he was 'really taken in by GM'; says Chrysler Corp engineers have told him that they could design and build ideal taxi for NYC if taxi owners would commit themselves to purchasing 3,000 cars each yr; praises Checker cabs and notes that more and more fleets are switching over to them; says he probably will leave comm 'in another year'; illus

headline: Sex Offenses Charged to Film Maker
abstract: A Sole, producer of film Deep Sleep, and actors M Canary and J Rose, who both appear in film, are charged on Jan 24 by Passaic County, NJ, prosecutor J D J Gorley with series of sexual offenses related to film; Gourley says it is 1st instance that he is aware of in which sexual charges were filed in connection with making of film; Sole is accused of having aided and abetted actors to commit fornication, conspiracy with them to commit in private acts of lewdness or carnal indecency and of having invited actors to place or bldg for purpose of lewdness; none of 3 charged have been arrested; illus of poster advertising film, currently showing in Wayne, NJ

headline: Johnson Buried at Texas Ranch
abstract: Pres Johnson is buried on Jan 25 on northern bank of Pedernales River next to graves of his parents on LBJ ranch; final service, with former Gov J B Connally and Rev B Graham speaking, is held at graveside; service is attended by neighbors and old friends; Rev W Schneider gives invocation; remarks by Connally and Graham noted; ceremony ends with Gen W C Westmoreland placing wreath, sent by Pres Nixon, at foot of coffin; officials attending service include Sen Humphrey, House Speaker Albert and former Atty Gen R Clark; illus of Johnson family while A Bryant sings Battle Hymn of the Repub; illus of family with Brig Gen J U Cross, who piloted Johnson's plane; illus of Connally and Graham

headline: Johnson Buried at Texas Ranch
abstract: STONEWALL, Tex., Jan. 25 — Lyndon Baines Johnson was buried today in a country graveyard on the northern bank of the Pedernales River. His coffin was lowered into the earth under an aged, twisted oak next to the graves of his mother and father on the former President's ranch.

headline: Widow of Johnson And Two Daughters Pay Visit to Grave

headline: ‘Deep Sleep’ Film Director Arraigned on 9 Charges

headline: Pakistani Parties Are Split Over Draft Constitution

headline: Topless Dancing Stirs Protest

headline: WOE MULTIPLYING FOR X‐RATED FILM
abstract: Passaic County, NJ, asst prosecutor J T Niccollai and other local officials are reptdly puzzled by FBI investigation of X-rated film Deep Sleep; film has run afoul of FBI in Oklahoma and Oklahoma City vice squad; Oklahoma City office of FBI on Feb 9 will ask US Magistrate's Ct to issue search warrant empowering bur to seize film as evidence of possible violation of Fed law prohibiting transportation of obscene matter; Oklahoma FBI on Jan 22 obtained restraining order prohibiting Oklahoma City theater from making any cuts in film or destroying any shipping documents; Oklahoma vice squad arrested and arraigned 2 members of theater mgt for showing lewd and obscene films; film's dir and producer A Sole repts he has not been questioned by FBI and says he wonders why they have been called into case

abstract: Byrne comments on how time can affect chess matches; drawing of indian defense

headline: Psychiatrists Review Stand on Homosexuals
abstract: Com of Amer Psychiatric Assn on Feb 8 begins deliberating on whether homosexuality should be considered form of mental illness and whether it ought to be stricken from assn's official catelogue of mental disorders; gay orgns have contended that psychiatry's continued recognition of homosexuality as mental disorder lends support to efforts to discriminate against homosexuals in business and govt; assn's Com on Nomenclature, which recommends revisions in catalog, hears members of Gay Activist Alliance present findings of med studies showing that many homosexuals are as well adjusted mentally as most heterosexuals; Assn V P Dr J Marmor says 'homosexuality in itself merely represents varient sexual preference which our soc disapproves of but which does not constitute mental illness'; Com Chmn Dr H Brill says some com members feel that in some cases homosexuality is central feature of a psychiatric problem

abstract: NYC's Bar Assn special com on sex and law and com on civil rights issue joint rept recommending passage by City Council of bill prohibiting discrimination against homosexuals in housing, employment and public accommodations

abstract: Marcus Welby, MD (TV Program): 6 members of Gay Activist Alliance on Feb 16 are arrested in ABC building, NYC, during sit-in protesting forthcoming Marcus Welby TV program in which homosexual is reptdly declared 'sick' and advised to see psychiatrist; ABC spokesman says episode will be shown as scheduled; alliance spokesman R Gold maintains episode is 'medically unsound' and 'filled with quackery'

headline: S.I. BLAST IS LAID TO TRAPPED GAS
abstract: Fire Chief O'Hagan, citing entrapment of gas behind Polyurethane tank lining as probable cause of Feb 10 fire and explosion at Tex Eastern Transmission's SI storage tank facility, says dept in future will allow only metal liners to be used in such tanks

headline: Rabbi and 2 Others to Run For Council in. Manhattan
abstract: Rabbi J G Neumann on Feb 19 announces that he will seek Dem nomination for NYC Council in new 3d Dist, covering lower Manhattan; C Choset, writer who asserts he is homosexual, repts he will seek Liberal party nomination for Councilman-at-Large seat from Manhattan; regular Liberal party nominee is H Stern; B A Rittersporn Jr, NY County Repub Volunteers pres, repts that he expects to bid for Repub nomination for Councilman-at-Large seat from Manhattan

headline: Judge Questions Four Charges Against ‘Deep Sleep’ Producer
abstract: Municipal Ct Judge E F Kushner on Feb 20 questions validity of 4 of 9 criminal charges that have been levied against A Sole because of sexual content of his x-rated film Deep Sleep; challenges counts against Sole that charge 'aiding and abetting acts of 'lewdness' and 'fornication' between actor J Rose and actress M Canary in Sole's home

headline: A Leader of Camden Draft Raid Appeals To Jury to ‘Ignore the Law’ and Acquit
abstract: Trial of 17 of Camden 28 begins in Camden Fed Dist Ct, Feb 27, following 3 weeks of jury selection; defendant P Grady asks jury to 'ignore law' and acquit antiwar activists of charges of destroying draft files, opening statement to jury; defendants' atty D Kairys adds defendants do not plan to deny charges, likening their actions to those of Dr M L King and D Ellsberg who 'employed civil disobedience to challenge questionable laws,' and citing historic cases of juries who sustained illegal actions; says FBI 'manufactured the crime' which was plotted and then abandoned 2 months before it was scheduled to take place, as defendants felt lack of expertise; adds acquaintance R W Hardy leaked revived version of plans, complete with diagrams, to FBI; Hardy has signed affidavit outlining role within Camden 28 and will not appear as Govt witness; defense plans to add claim of innocence on basis of entrapment to plea; Judge C S Fisher extends until Mar 1 order to release Mr and Mrs D B Grumbles, jailed for 14 months for contempt, but slated for release on Feb 27

headline: Gay Activists Say Police Hamper Protest Plan
abstract: Gay Activist Alliance spokesman R Gold on Feb 27 says that NYC police have denied permission for orgn to hold demonstration directly outside NY Hilton Hotel to protest annual Inner Circle dinner on Mar 3; says police have confined rally to site across st; says this violates apparent understanding, reached earlier at City Hall meeting, that would have allowed picketing and leaflets to be distributed at hotel's entrances; Police Dept spokesman says that demonstrations outside of midtown hotels are almost always held, for safety reasons, at distance of at least 1 block; alliance members and supporters contend justice was not done after '72 dinner when several men who disrupted proceedings were beaten by Uniformed Firefighters Assn pres M J Maye; Maye was later acquitted of harassment charges; list of supporters of protest

headline: 4 Women Get Into the Act In Reporters' Show Here
abstract: Inner Circle holds 51st annual lampoon show in NY Hilton; members of Gay Activists Alliance demonstrate outside Hilton calling for City Council passage of law regarding homosexual rights; other activities at Hilton noted

headline: WEST SIDE KEEPS VIGIL OVER PUPILS
abstract: Manhattan's West Side schools continue security precautions on Mar 12 following last wk's homosexual murder of 10-yr-old L Ortiz; parents conduct voluntary escort services for pupils going to and from school; police ptl are stationed at key corners; teachers and security guards maintain watch on corridors and playgrounds; students at PS 165, which victim attended, are reptd to be much calmer after showing great anxiety last wk

headline: Christopher Isherwood: No Parades
abstract: Goodbye to Berlin author C Isherwood discusses his homosexuality as revealed in autobiographical novel Kathleen and Frank, int; says idea of declaring homosexuality in print 'seems so wonderfully simple' it should ease other homosexual writers' doubts about declaring position; acknowledges usefulness of women's movement and gay movement, but prefers role of non-activist, 'using sr citizen respectability...and talking to others about their gayness'

headline: Monetary Evolution
abstract: ed says that finance mins and central bankers are properly concerned about world monetary system, even though dollar has moved up against most currencies and start of floating world seems stable and orderly enough; notes improvised solution could degenerate into wild exch-rate fluctuations, currency or trade wars among nations, or fresh raid on existing currency values by speculators; says differences and uncertainties among finance mins are still too great for prompt codification of new monetary system; notes communique issued in Washington by Com of 20 deputies is collection of 'vague generalities' while most important in declaration is pronouncement that new exch-rate regime should remain based on stable but adjustable par values; says this seems to mean that some mins are still worried about system with too much flexibility while others think greater flexibility is essential to new order; says best thing about Com of 20 meeting is that it really did nothing to reverse progress already made toward developing more flexible monetary order

headline: CHURCHES EXPAND FOR HOMOSEXUALS
abstract: Universal Fellowship of Met Community Chs, rapidly expanding denomination of homosexual chs founded in '68, has helped establish the 1st 'gay' synagogue and plans to apply in '74 for membership in Natl Council of Chs; repts it has 43 congregations in 19 states and London and internatl membership of 15,000; Rev T D Perry, founding pastor, says he anticipates no theological problems over council's membership requirements; preaches need for personal salvation through belief in Christ; asserts his congregations are interested in charismatic movement or pentecostal experience of faith healing, speaking in tongues and prophecy; homosexual synagogue is also seeking membership in Union of Amer Hebrew Congregations; union's dir Rabbi E Herman says 'chances are excellent' that synagogue will be accepted when it applies for membership; acknowledges that there will be resistance to group, particularly among the rabbinate; both ch and synagogue congregations, which shared ch bldg in Los Angeles, were forced out when fire of 'suspicious origin' caused $150,000 worth of damage Jan 27

headline: Juvenile Justice: Failures in the System of Detention
abstract: L Oelsner series on NYC juvenile justice system describes Spofford Juvenile Center, NYC's maximum security detention center for children; NY Times study of city's juvenile insts found that they are characterized by high recidivism, homosexuality, inadequate treatment, poorly trained staff and other signs of failure; even prison officials concede that insts can harm children that enter them; conditions at city's other juvenile insts, Callagy Hall, Jennings Hall and Children's Center, noted; illus

headline: City Considers Fencing Washington Square Park
abstract: ?? plained that their renowned park, a magnet for the city's cultural underground on sunny Sunday mornings, has been swamped with derelicts, narcotics addicts and sexual perverts. Some residents say they have stopped going intd the park, even during the day.

headline: THIEU, M. TEXAS, HONORS JOHNSON
abstract: S Vietnam Pres Nguyen Van Thieu lays wreath at grave of late Pres Johnson on Apr 7 at cemetery near Stonewall, Tex; Thieu is accompanied by Mrs Johnson, family members and others; private luncheon follows; illus

headline: Mr. Nixon's Power Grab
abstract: T Wicker comment on Pres Nixon's 'power grab' notes Atty Gen Kleindienst's recent claim that all 2.5-million Fed employes can be directed by Pres not to testify before Cong and believes it is example of how need for strong exec govt can be perverted into open grab for imperial powers; cites examples of what he considers 'low intellectual and const level' of Kleindienst's performance'; notes other Nixon Adm attempts to achieve raw and unchecked power; cartoon

headline: Two City Policemen Are Found Guilty Of An Extortion Plot
abstract: NYC police detective J Busch and ptl W McKeon are found guilty on Apr 13, NYS Sup Ct, of charges of plotting to extort money from S Resnick, owner of tavern where small amount of narcotics were found in '72

headline: Evelyn Waugh Diary: A Life Revisited
abstract: Brit writer E Waugh, appearing in weekly installments of Observer (GB) causes anxiety among author's friends; diaries tell of world of twenties and thirties, affording insight into Waugh's friendships and work; illus

headline: Princeton Likes ‘Perverto’ Slate
abstract: Slate of 4 Princeton Univ students, promising electorate 'mindless perversion,' is given good chance of victory in Apr 18 Undergrad Assembly races; 4 outdistanced both of 2 more conservative slates in recent primary; Perverto candidate for pres, R Goodman, says 'we have nothing to offer...all we have is rampant desire to pervert'; outgoing Assembly pres J Carples asserts that Perverto slate's popularity is due to broad dissatisfaction with student pol; other candidates score Perverto ticket as dangerous joke; Goodman notes Perverto campaign got its start from '72 statement by univ pres Dr W G Bowen in which he referred to 'occasional and no doubt healthy touch of perversity that characterizes student body'; Goodman and 2d Perverto candidate C Hayden illus

headline: Supreme Court Limits ‘Entrapment’ Defense in Upholding Conviction of Amphetamine Dealer on Coast
abstract: US Sup Ct, 5-4, on Apr 24 upholds narcotics conviction of R Russell, who mfrd amphetamines on order of undercover Fed agent, who also provided him with chem ingredients essential to produce product

headline: Suspect in 6 Rapes Here Is Sentenced for Robbery
abstract: R Carbone, indicted in 6 rape cases in Nov, '72 after look-alike L Berson was jailed for 11 days and then freed, is sentenced on Apr 25 to up to 20 yrs for robbery; was allowed to plead guilty on Mar 21 to 8 charges of robbery to cover indictments that also included forced sodomy, kidnapping, weapons possession and grand larceny; Women's Anti-Rape Group pickets outside courthouse to protest dropping of rape charges in plea-bargaining process; if Carbone had been convicted on original indictment, he could have received up to 30 yrs in concurrent sentences, or up to 225 yrs in consecutive sentences; case revd

headline: Council Body to V ote Today, Third Time, On Homosexual Bill
abstract: NYC City Council's Gen Welfare Com will vote Apr 27 on twice-defeated bill to bar discrimination against homosexuals in housing, employment and public accommodations

headline: City Council Committee Rejects Homosexual Bill
abstract: NYC City Council's Gen Welfare Com on Apr 27 refuses to vote out bill to ban discrimination against homosexuals in housing, employment and public accommodations; action is 3d such setback for bill in last 2 yrs; Gay Activists Alliance stages demonstration over dismay at vote; Mayor Lindsay calls vote 'disappointment'

headline: Entrapment
abstract: Comment on Apr 24 Sup Ct decision on use of entrapment to catch criminals in action revs history of legal decisions involving question; decision came in case of R Russell, from whom undercover narcotics agent ordered amphetamines, promising to provide Russell with scarce chemical element so that he could mfr drug

headline: TWO NIXON AIDES EXPECTED TO SEE U.S. PROSECUTORS
abstract: Sources close to Watergate case say White House aides H R Haldeman and J D Ehrlichman will meet with Fed prosecutors to discuss their possible roles in Watergate break-in and subsequent cover-up; summoning of Haldeman and Ehrlichman to meeting with chief Govt prosecutor, E J Silbert, is seen as 1st formal sign that they are under investigation by grand jury; Haldeman is known to be under inquiry to determine whether his office had role in initial bugging operation or any subsequent attempts to obstruct investigation; Ehrlichman was cited by L P Gray 3d, former FBI Acting Dir, as being present at meeting 11 days after Watergate break-in at which Gray was handed file containing documents belonging to one of Watergate participants and strongly urged to make sure files 'never see the light of day'; Gray has said man who handed files to him was White House counsel J W Dean 3d; Washington Post repts that Dean intends to swear under oath that he was ordered by Haldeman and Ehrlichman to coordinate cover-up and reptd regularly on its progress to them; other Watergate developments include Time (pub) rept that former White House counsel C W Colson recruited young men during '72 Pres campaign to pose as homosexual supporters of Dem Sen McGovern in attempt to link McGovern with 'gay liberation' cause; Colson denies this and other Time rept which says J S Magruder, former deputy chief of Nixon re-election com, told Fed prosecutors that Colson knew about Watergate plans in advance and even urged in telephone call to Magruder that they be expedited; Sen Percy says in TV int that he will introduce Sen resolution calling on Pres Nixon to appt pol independent prosecutor for Watergate case; Sen Weicker, member of Sen Watergate com, sharply criticizes what he calls implications made by White House that FBI Acting Dir L P Gray 3d was forced out; Weicker says Gray made his own decision

headline: 8 Indicted in ‘Boys‐for‐Sale’ Ring
abstract: 8 men, including former organizer for Big Brothers of NY H Oelke and child psychiatrist Dr M Fraser, are indicted on May 3 in connection with internatl homosexual ring that operated out of Suffolk County (NY); 2-yr investigation determined that ring supplied boys as young as 10 yrs old as part of club; links with Big Brother orgn are still under investigation, including possible fraudulent use of group's name by members of homosexual ring to attract children and reassure parents; operation of ring described; men arecharged with conspiracy, sodomy and sexual abuse; others are identified as: L McGaw, Sheridan Coll (Ont) prof; C Slavin; G Brehm; G Rossman, dean of Ecumenical Continuing Educ Center of New Haven; A Riviezzo and R Ramos

headline: Unfair Entrapment
abstract: Ed discusses recent Sup Ct decision to turn back attempt to limit police power to entrap potential criminals by encouraging them to commit crime for which only disposition may have existed; cites hearings into case of Camden 28 which revealed FBI use of 'agent provocateur' in supplying R Hardy with means of committing crime, recalling FBI's earlier promise to Hardy that crime would be stemmed before its execution; warns entrapment techniques that push dissenters over the line are dangerous subversion of police power

headline: Doctors Urged Not to Call Homosexuality Illness
abstract: Amer Psychiatric Assn meets, May 9

headline: The Life To Come
abstract: Forster, E M: Book The Life to Come And Other Short Stories, by E M Forster, revd by E Welty; illus

headline: U.S. TACTIC SCORED AT CAMDEN TRIAL
abstract: Camden 28 defense atty D Kairys tells jury on May 15 that group is depending on concept of ‘overreaching Govt participation’ in form of help received from ‘agent provocateur’ R Hardy to ensure defendants’ acquittal; Judge C S Fisher had informed defense that jury findings of either entrapment or overreaching would be adequate grounds for acquittal; Kairys informs jury that defendents do not claim entrapment as they were predisposed to commit crime before FBI provided means; asst atty J J Barry notes case could be 1st in which judge instructs jury that such overreaching constitutes grounds for acquittal, int

headline: Cub Scoutmaster Accused Of Molesting Boy in Pack
abstract: Bedford‐Stuyvesant Cub Scout leader F Moddica is arrested on May 14 and arraigned on charges of sodomy involving boys in his pack

headline: A revisionist view of female sexuality
abstract: book Our Bodies, Ourselves, A Book by and For Women, by the Boston Women's Health Book Collective, revd by E Lester

headline: Johnson's Herefords Sold for High Prices
abstract: cattlemen on May 21 pay $140,560 for prize Hereford herd of late Pres Johnson; auctioneer R Reyes says cattle drew high prices because of demand 'not the LBJ name'

headline: Prisons
abstract: article on growing trend toward prisons having both male and female inmates comments on announcement that female‐male facility will open in Conn in '76; plans for inst detailed; proponents of mixed incarceration hold that situation improves motivation and behavior as well as promoting decline in homosexuality and changing atmosphere conducive to riots; illus

headline: The Nation
abstract: Recent agreement between Public Broadcasting Corp and Public Broadcasting Service over who shall control public TV programing revd; illus

headline: ... the C.I.A....
abstract: ed says memorandums prepared by CIA officiais published in NY Times on June 4 spell out in painfully clear detail Nixon Adm's effort to pervert CIA for its own domestic pol purposes; notes that in 1st of memos, CIA Deputy Dir Walters discusses what then-CIA Dir Helms told H R Haldeman and J D Ehrlichman in Ehrlichman's office June 23 '72; quotes Walters as saying 'Helms said he had talked to Gray (then-Acting FBI Dir) on previous day and made plain to him that the agency (CIA) was not behind this matter and that it was not connected with it. None of suspects was working for it nor had worked for agency in the last 2 yrs. He had told Gray that none of his investigators was touching any covert projects of the agency, current or ongoing'; says in any properly run Adm, this definitive statement from CIA head should have ended any further discussion; says question arises as to why White House did not convey its instructions directly to Gray; says Nixon's responsibility for this perversion of CIA is heavy; says since Haldeman was Nixon's chief aide and since only Pres can command CIA, authority behind instructions is evident

headline: Do We Dare Help the Artist Who Dares?
abstract: Rockefeller Foundation Arts Dir H Klein discusses work of foundations in promoting music, theater, dance, literature, art and photography; some recipients listed; illus

headline: Parliament in Bonn Eases Sex and Pornography Laws
abstract: W Ger Govt lifts tech ban on wife‐swapping and has eased other 19th century laws on sex; new law, approved in Bundestag by vote of 254‐203, lowers permissible age limit for homosexual acts between consenting males from 21 to 18; permits restricted sale of pornography; restricts violence on TV programs to protect minors

headline: Advertising: Moscow Missions
abstract: A Pellini of Haworth Press announces plans to publish Journal of Homosexuality

headline: Screen: 'The Last of Sheila' Arrives at the Sutton:Murder Mystery Puts Fun Into Format The Cast Turns Search for' Killer Into a Cruise Game
abstract: Riviera yacht guests and murder. Blandness does it in.

headline: Morris County Prisoners Tell What's Right and Wrong in Jail
abstract: Morris County Jail (NJ) is opened to reporters on June 14; inmates complain about lack of jail personnel and outdoor recreation and frequency of sodomy incidents; praise guards, med supervision, improvement in food and increase in privileges

headline: 14 Policemen in Baltimore Indicted in Numbers Case
abstract: 14 Baltimore policemen and 19 civilians are indicted on June 14 on charges involving payoffs to protect illegal numbers operations in city; 5 lts, 6 sgts 2 ptl and vice squad detective are policemen indicted

headline: EASED DRUG LAWS OPPOSED IN JERSEY
abstract: Proposals to 'decriminalize' use and possession of marijuana in NJ runs into opposition on June 15 from legislators studying possibility of amending state's narcotics laws; both appeal for ending criminal sanctions against 'recreational' or 'occasional' use of marijuana; stiff resistance to such reform comes during hearing in Newark by State Legis Comm to Study Drug Law Penalties and Treatment Programs: recommendations by 4 reprs of Natl Orgn for Reform of Marijuana Laws that criminal penalties be ended for use and possession of 'small amounts' of marijuana is assailed by 3 comm members; Arlington, Va, pediatrician Dr D V Whipple testifies in favor of decriminalization; contends persent laws against marijuana are 'more than failure' and are 'a positive harm'; notes laws are 'ignored' by 26-million users of marijuana in US and that 'a whole generation is growing up with the belief that laws they do not like can be broken with impunity'; maintains few marijuana users who are apprehended and convicted 'suffer out of all proportion to their crimes'; Fed Govt's objections to decriminalization of marijuana recalled

headline: Theater: The Faggot,'
abstract: A Carmines play The Faggot revd by C Barnes

headline: Research Rescuing A Trapped Minisub
abstract: article revs events leading to entrapment of Sea‐Link research submarine in wreck of destroyer F T Berry and traces series of rescue plans evolved in attempt to free vessel; submarine illus; diagram showing Sea‐Link's position on destroyer on ocean floor

headline: Homosexuals March Down 7th Avenue
abstract: Thousands of homosexuals and supporters of homosexuals on June 24 march in 4th annual Christopher St Liberation Day parade in NYC; march coincides with last day of Gay Pride Week, commemg night of June 27, '68 when group of homosexuals resisted police raid by rioting outside bar frequented by homosexuals, the Stonewall Inn, on Christopher St; groups such as Gay Activists Alliance and Mattachine Soc are represented; illus

headline: Arson Suspected in Deaths of 29 in New Orleans Bar
abstract: New Orleans police are investigating possibility of arson by a disgruntled customer in June 24 French Qr fire that killed 28 men and a woman and injured 15 in Upstairs (bar); some of the survivors strongly suspect fire was set by one or two men evicted from bar less than an hour before the fire; fire, lasting only 16 mins, burned so hot in the second‐floor bar that the bodies of the victims were cooked together in a pile; most of those who died were trying to reach 3 windows at the front of the bldg; Upstairs, described by neighbors as a lavish homosexual bar, was packed with men who had come for the weekly, Sunday night 'beer bust'; illus

headline: For S.R.O. Hotel Roomers, It's a Precarious Life
abstract: Article on Kimberly, Manhattan Towers, Towers West, Benjamin Franklin and Belle Claire Hotels, single-room-occupany hotels on Upper West Side, Manhattan, that cater to welfare recipients; discusses deterioration of area, which is scene of homicides, prostitution, drug addiction and homosexuality; cites security measures taken by Manhattan Towers mgt to alleviate previous problems; notes Soc Services Dept pays about $30 a wk for each welfare client's rent; adds welfare referrals, on which Manhattan Towers has depended, were suspended last winter because of inadequate bldg security, but referrals have now resumed; map; illus

headline: COURT REVERSES BERRIGAN RULINGS
abstract: 3-judge panel at Phila Fed Appeals Ct on June 27 reverses conviction on 6 of 7 counts of smuggling lrs in and out of Lewisburg prison levied against Rev P F Berrigan and Mrs Berrigan (formerly Sister E McAlister), on grounds that law prohibits sending of lrs without 'knowledge and consent' of warden; ct explains warden was aware in all but 1 case that lrs were being carried by inmate informer B Douglas; reversal on 3 of 4 counts in Berrigan's case constitutes only moral and technical victory, while reversal of decision against Sister Elizabeth means she is freed from serving 1-yr term levied against her and from 3-yr suspended sentence slated to begin at end of prison term; P O'Dwyer, who served along with R Clark as appellants' lawyer, says decision was expected and is merely technical, telephone int; ct took pains to explain it did not consider convictions outgrowth of 'entrapment,' or Fed plot to draw defendants into illegal activity through use of informant

headline: Screen:' Cleopatra Jones' Treks to Drug Netherworld
abstract: Federal agent Jones tries to rescue her framed boyfriend from drug-queen pervert known as Mommy.

headline: The Sinking Dollar
abstract: Ed says one tangible cause of drop in confidence in Amer dollar stems from Watergate affair, which has deepened skepticism about ability of Nixon Adm to govern effectively

headline: Sabotaging the G.O.P.'s Rivals: Story of a $100,000 Operation
abstract: while Segretti was still recruiting spies, and unknown to him, a separate sabotage campaign was underway, managed by J S Magruder, deputy dir of re-election com, with some direction from then special counsel to Pres, C W Colson; Magruder has described it as attempt to gether 'as much information (as possible) through sources in opposition's com'; H L Porter, re-election com scheduling dir, was assigned by Magruder to recruit intelligence operatives and dole out cash for projects which were suggested mainly by Colson, according to 1 re-election com official; Colson denies his reptd sponsorship of plan to send someone to NH before Pres primary and contribute $200 to campaign of Repr P N McCloskey Jr in name of Gay Liberation Front, in hope of having fact published in pro-Nixon Manchester Union-Leader, thereby linking McCloskey with militant homosexual orgn; Porter has told Sen Watergate com he disbursed nearly $70,000 in cash at Magruder's request, including additional $31,000 to G G Liddy for unspecified 'dirty tricks' and $4,400 for another Colson project--purchase of full-page ad in NY Times purported to represent grassroots support for mining of Haiphong Harbor; Porter also paid for pickets to harass Sen Muskie at campaign stops; 1 operative who infiltrated Muskie campaign provided Porter with photograph of memorandum by Muskie's polling expert, A Navarro, suggesting that Muskie hold hearings of Intergovt Relations subcom, which he headed, to 'take advantage of free TV time' before he announced his candidacy; memo was retyped and sent to syndicated columnists R Evans and R Novak, their reprinting of memo was 'very damaging' to Muskie, according to an aide of his; illus of Chapin, Segretti, Colson and Magruder

headline: Homosexuality Ruled No Basis for Bar Rejection
abstract: NYS Appeals Ct has recently ruled, in 6-to-1 vote, that homosexual lawyer H L Kimball cannot be denied admission to NYS bar solely on grounds of his homosexuality; ordered reconsideration of Kimball's application by Appellate Div, which denied Kimball admission to bar on Jan 8 on grounds that '55 arrest on sodomy charge and his admitted homosexuality made him unfit to practice law in NYS; Kimball's legal career and present case revd

headline: PSYCHOSURGERY CURBED BY COURT
abstract: Judges H W Gilmore, G E Bowles and J D O'Hair, in precedent-setting decision, on July 10 rule that experimental psychosurgery may not be performed on persons confined against their will in state insts, even when person's consent is formally obtained, Wayne County (Detroit) Circuit Ct; decision leaves way open for performance of psychosurgery on such persons once procedure has advanced to level where its benefits clearly outweigh its risks; judges contend that is not currently the case, given the primitive state of current knowledge of the brain; decision applies to brain surgery in cases where there is abnormal behavior, and at same time, 'demonstrable physical abnormality in the brain' but in which no connection between abnormality and behavior has yet been established; decision does not apply to widely accepted surgical treatments for such clearly defined physical-mental syndromes as epilepsy, Parkinson's disease or stroke; case on which ruling is based involves 36-yr-old male mental patient, who was committed to Ionia State Hosp in '55 after he was charged with raping and murdering a nurse; he was classified as 'criminal sexual psychopath'; he agreed in '72 to be subject of psychosurgery as part of experiment at Lafayette Clinic; suit was brought in his behalf by civil liberties lawyer G Kaimowitz; early in trial, judges declared that patient was being confined unconstitutionally under law repealed in '68; he is now free, undergoing conventional psychotherapy; psychosurgery procedure and its results described

headline: Homosexual London Guide
abstract: London Tourist Bd backs free tourist guide that caters to young homosexuals and gives advice on VD; guide was compiled by youth advice center for young people

headline: Child Psychiatrist Arrested 2d Time On Morals Charge
abstract: Suffolk County, NY, child psychiatrist M Krassner on July 13 is arrested and charged with child abuse for 2d time in 2 mos; is released on $500 bail after being charged with sexual abuse of 10‐yr‐old girl; earlier case revd

headline: The Gay Life: Cartoon vs. Reality?
abstract: M Duberman revs A Carmines play The Faggot and J Katz play Coming Out!, both of which deal with theme of homosexuality

headline: N.F.L. Suspends Rentzel
abstract: NFL comr Rozelle discloses on July 24 that Los Angeles Rams football player L Rentzel has been suspended for '73 season for conduct detrimental to NFL; Rentzel has been under league probation after being indicted for indecent exposure and on another occasion for possession of marijuana

headline: Drama Mailbag
abstract: lr by A Carmines, author and dir of play The Faggot, on M Duberman's July 22 comment on play's effect on homosexual community in NYC; Carmines illus

headline: Homosexual Family Units
abstract: Homosexual couples have been recognized as family units by Mass Red Cross Blood Program; about 100 pints of blood were donated this weekend by such couples after Red Cross issued emergency appeal; couples are now eligible to receive blood from program for any children of either partner

headline: Rentzel Case Taken to Court
abstract: NFL Players' Assn discloses on July 30 that it will seek an injunction in Calif cts on Aug 1 restraining NFL comr Rozelle from suspending Los Angeles Rams football player L Rentzel; Rentzel was suspended for conduct detrimental to NFL after being convicted of indecent exposure and possession of marijuana; case revd; Rentzel por

headline: Getting To Know Anyone
abstract: R Keyes article discusses difficulty of developing personal intimacy in modern Amer, where people change residences so often and guard privacy so jealously that 'sustained human contact becomes almost impossible'; sees Amers seeking closeness without entrapment, as evidenced in casual sex mores; holds sex, rather than occurring after intimacy is attained, is now used to promote intimacy

headline: Pro Football's Position
abstract: Do two arrests for indecent exposure and one for drug possession represent a player's lifestyle?

headline: Port Authority Reports 18,000 Crimes in 1972
abstract: Port Auth of NY and NJ Policemen's Benevolent Assn, in move to discourage replacement of police at Hudson River crossings with civilians, on Aug 7 release statistics showing that over 18,000 crimes were committed at auth facilities in '72; rept, which members of assn say is confidential, lists 711 murders, 10 rapes, 245 armed robberies, 157 unarmed robberies and 166 assaults; shows that 5 murders, 3 rapes, 77 armed robberies, 23 cases of indecent exposure and 167 narcotic arrests occurred at auth's bus terminal at 41st St and 8th Av

headline: Youth, 17, and Ex‐Convict Held in ‘Thrill Killing’
abstract: 17-yr-old S Zada and ex-convict R F Cortez are accused on Aug 8 of possible 'thrill killing' of dance teacher J B Stout, whose body was found in Spring Valley, NY, apt on July 20; Cortez, Zada and F W Gensel Jr are currently under indictment for holdup-murder of wealthy plumbing contractor C Gunther on July 14 in South Nyack; no motive has been found for murder of Stout, an admitted homosexual; Zada and Cortez also were known to associate with homosexuals

headline: Mrs. Gandhi Calls India's Crisis ‘Passing Phase’ and Asks Calm
abstract: Indian Prime Min Gandhi on Aug 9 says difficulties confronting India are only 'passing phase' and that there is 'no cause for panic', speech to natl convention of Indians who had worked for independence from GB; says that there is 'big attempt' to make her Govt and people 'deviate from path of socialism'; says certain forces are creating difficulties, but 'we will fight such forces and succeed'; does not identify these forces, but it is apparent that she is referring to opposition parties that have been agitating about prevailing food shortage, rising prices and unemployment; mob violence over prices has been reptd in several parts of nation; there are 7.5-million unemployed persons in India, increase of 1-million since Aug '72; Govt critics are gaining support and becoming vociferous as Gandhi attempts to deal with many crises; Pres V V Giri recently criticized Govt to delight of opposition

headline: HOMOSEXUALS GET POLICE PROMISES
abstract: 200 homosexuals march on 10th Police Pct hq in Chelsea sec of Manhattan on Aug 9 to protest alleged police harassment; Gay Activists Alliance pres B Voeller charges that 2 homosexuals were recently harassed and beaten by police without provocation; acting pct comdr Capt R Boetig says both cases are under rev by Civilian Complaint Rev Bd; says there is no deliberate policy of harassment; promises that policemen would in future meet with leaders of homosexual community in effort to ease tensions

headline: Texan Said to Admit Role in 25 Killings
abstract: Houston police say on Aug 9 that 17-yr-old E W Henley told them that he and D A Corll were involved in more than 25 slayings; bodies of 17 teen-agers have been uncovered in rented boat shed, and 2 more are uncovered near lake development 120 mi to northeast; Henley said he killed Corll, whom he describes as 'sexual pervert', after Corll threatened to kill him and 2 other young people after sniffing paint at his house; Henley had originally said Corll had committed all the murders, but now admits having taken part in slayings, which took place over 3-yr period; some bodies are found in plastic bags, some are in graves covered with lime, some are unclothed; police say victims may have been tortured to death; identifications of 2 bodies are confirmed as M R Jones, 18, and C C Cobble, 17; illus

headline: Texas Police Find Four More Bodies; The Total Is Now 23
abstract: 4 more badly decomposed bodies are unearthed near Houston on Aug 10, bringing to 23 the number of victims allegedly sexually assaulted, tortured and slain over 3-yr period by D A Corll and 2 accomplices, 17-yr-old E W Henley and D O Brooks, 18; Brooks came forward on Aug 10 and admitted observing some of slayings and helping to dispose of some of bodies; police say Henley and Brooks had recruited young boys for 'parties' at Corll's house, at which boys would be given acrylics to sniff and sometimes marijuana; then they would be stripped, bound to board with handcuffs and straps, and forced to commit sodomy and other sexual acts before being tortured and strangled or shot; Henley and Brooks were allegedly paid $5 to $10 by Corll for each youth; Brooks tells police of being promised and receiving car from Corll in exchange for keeping silent after he witnessed party slaying; 1 of bodies found on Aug 10 is identified as W R Lawrence, 15, by his father; Henley has been charged with 3 counts of murder in St Augustine County; charges against Henley and Brooks in Houston are being prepared; illus; map

headline: Gains Reported in Drive Against Vice in Midtown
abstract: NYC mayoral task force's 2d qrly rept released on Aug 10 says that city's continuing drive against vice in Times Sq area shows signs of success with closing of more massage parlors; repts 50% drop in number of prostitutes operating in area; says 12 of 20 massage parlors have been closed since April and legal action is pending against 6 of remaining 8; police note that clean-up campaign has resulted in change in prostitute population in area from white to black; say that white girls have gone to East Side, outside area of Times Square drive; vice arrest figures for 2d qr

headline: 2 Youths Indicted in Texas Killings
abstract: E W Henley and D O Brooks, who confessed they participated in homosexual torture slayings of 27 boys by D A Corll, are indicted for murder on Aug 14 by Harris County grand jury; Henley is indicted in death of C C Cobble and M R Jones; Brooks is charged along with Henley in murder of W R Lawrence; grand jury hears testimony from B Ridinger, 20, who went to and from grand jury room with paper sack over his head with holes cut for eyes, and who told grand jury that he barely escaped death in murders; illus

headline: Alleged Homosexual Ring Found In a Raid on Apartment in Dallas
abstract: Odyssey House, NYC‐based drug rehabilitation program, spokesman James Murphy expresses shock at use of name Odyssey Foundation by nationwide homosexual procurement ring discovered Aug 14 in Dallas; denies having any connection with group; Gay Activists Alliance official R Gold says he has never heard of group

headline: CAWLEY TO PRESS GRAFT DETECTION
abstract: NYC Police Comr Cawley on Aug 23 unveils master plan for improving Police Dept by giving high priority to new anti‐corruption measures, faster police response to emergency calls and recruitment of more minority group members as policemen; many of 42 projects have been previously announced and some have been implemented on experimental basis; plan directs various dept anti‐corruption units to initiate investigations rather than acting only on specific complaints; program has been devised to test integrity of officers who are suspected of corrupt activities by placing them in position to engage in corrupt activities, without entrapment, so that their responses may be observed; plans also call for reorganization of detective force, increased services to youthful offenders, development of computerized crime‐analysis program, and improvements in communications, training and pct mgt

headline: Nixon Honoys Johnson
abstract: Black wreath from Pres Nixon is placed on grave of late Pres Johnson during memorial ceremonies on Aug 26; Aug 27 would have been Johnson's 65th birthday

headline: Mayor Rizzo of Philadelphia, Beset by Growing Problems and Disputes, Finds Himself at a Crisis Point
abstract: Philadelphia (Pa) Mayor F L Rizzo is viewed at crisis point in his short but flamboyant pol career; has been accused of employing special 33‐member squad of city police to spy on and harass his pol opponents, including City Council Pres G X Schwartz and city Dem leader P J Camiel, and of offering bribe to Camiel, who is now his biggest pol foe; has managed, during his 1 1/2 yrs in City Hall, to attack or alienate at one time or another many powerful city leaders; most damaging of all to Rizzo, whose pol career has been built in large measure on his image as man who is blunt, tough, honest and incorruptible, is news that he apparently lied on 6 of 10 questions put to him in public polygraph test administered by expert hired by Philadelphia Daily News; test, which grew out of exchange of allegations between Rizzo and Camiel dealt with charges that Rizzo had offered Camiel control over certain lucrative city contracts; Camiel maintained that Rizzo, in return, wanted his support as Dem leader for candidate Rizzo was backing for Dist Atty; allegation spurred lie detector episode; Camiel had alleged that Rizzo approached him with offer in men's room of Bellevue Stratford Hotel on Feb 27; also present was Deputy Mayor P Carroll; both Rizzo and Carroll denied that any deal had been offered; Daily News proposed lie detector scheme; all 3 principals agree to answer questions; results, according to polygraph expert W D Holmes, indicated that Rizzo and Carroll had lied on 6 of 10 questions and Camiel on none

headline: HOMOSEXUAL NINE LOSES TO POLICE
abstract: NYC Police Softball team from 6th Pct on Aug 27 defeats team sponsored by NY Mattachine Soc and composed of homosexual men and women; over $1,000 was raised in donations to One‐to‐One program for retarded children; game grew out of weekly rap sessions held between police and leaders of homosexual community since Nov ‘72

headline: ‘We Are Already Your Children’
abstract: A Kantrowitz article contrasts growing respect and equality among all Amer immigrant and minority groups with the suppression of homosexuality; contends emergence of homosexual affection as accepted fact of Amer life is simply 1 more element of variety in Amer's natl identity; cites existence of homosexuality among all peoples of Amer as challenge to Amer ideals

headline: Meany Is Critical of Nixon On Economy and Election
abstract: G Meany, in wide-ranging pre-Labor Day speech, says AFL-CIO will be able to reach agreement with Teamsters union in regard to dispute between C Chavez and Teamsters; under such accord, Teamsters will give up their contracts to represent agr workers in Calif and let Chavez and United Farm Workers Organizing Com continue to try to organize field workers there

headline: In Singapore, a super‐pimp awaits beatification

headline: MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO SEX ABUSE OF BOY

headline: Homosexual Films Ruffle Businessmen on 44th St.
abstract: Controversy has arisen over showing of 'adult' and 'male' films by Little Theater on 44th St between 7th and 8th Avs, Manhattan; protests come from theatrical producers, restauranteurs and owners of legitimate theaters in area; Bway producer A H Cohen says 'we will drive the vermin away'; concern has been expressed that traditional character of block will be affected by pornography shows; Cohen says that theatrical community will mount campaign to shut down Little Theater; illus

headline: The Pierrepont: A Brooklyn Horror House
abstract: Article on Pierrepont Hotel in Bklyn, where prostitutes, pimps, drug addicts and derelicts run rampant; neighborhood residents complain of fights, knifings and of being mugged in their doorways across from hotel; elderly residents of hotel live in fear of undesirables who frequent establishment, but also in fear of harassment and eviction by hotel mgt; police rept 36 founded complaints and 7 arrests in or near hotel since Jan 1; homosexual club rents 3 floors of hotel; illus

headline: Ex‐City Official Says He's Homosexual
abstract: Dr H J Brown, Lindsay adm's 1st Health Services Admr, on Oct 2 openly acknowledges his homosexuality in effort to end prejudice homosexuals face in obtaining employment, int; to make same statement in address on Oct 3 to 600 physicians at symposium on human sexuality at Carrier Clinic, Belle Mead, NJ; disclosed that he was homosexual 3 wks ago before bd of dirs of Public Health Assn; calls it 'tribute to bd' that following his declaration he was apptd chmn of com to combat discrimination against homosexuals in health community; says he knows of homosexual priests, clergymen, dentists and politicians and several other Comrs who were homosexuals during period he served; attributes his decision to disclose his homosexuality to sharp decline in public hostility toward homosexuals; says he made decision to resign adm post only when he learned that late columnist D Pearson might be writing column about homosexual Lindsay comrs; left adm in '67 after 18 mos as dir of health services program; is currently on faculty of NYU Med School; por

headline: Doctors Called Ignorant of Sex Mores
abstract: NJ Med Soc and NJ Psychiatric Assn sponsor all-day seminar on Oct 3 titled Human Sexuality Today at Carrier Clinic, Belle Meade, NJ; conf is attempt to bring physician 'a little up to date' and to get physicians to 'take fresh look at themselves and their beliefs' on sex; Dr R J Cross says that avg Amer 'regards his physician as expert in sexuality and avg physician has no knowledge in sexuality'; Dr R S Garber says avg dr will usually refer his patients' sexual problems to psychiatrist 'because they have such fear and dread of their inability to treat these problems'; Dr H J Brown, former Lindsay adm cabinet member who has revealed that he is practicing homosexual, is guest speaker; notes most homosexuals are 'fearful of revealing their homosexual behavior and will use physician known to be homosexual, if one is available'; says he intends to become 'militant' homosexual and march in demonstrations and, if necessary, be arrested

abstract: STONEWALL, Tex., Oct. 11 —The towering stalks of yellow Maximilian daisies planted as a part of Mrs. Lyndon B. Johnson's highway beautification program decorated highways leading to the Lyndon B. Johnson State Park Thursday.

headline: INDIAN SECT STIRS A BITTER DISPUTE
abstract: Indian Govt contends that Anand Marg Soc, controversial yoga group, is violent, potentially dangerous cult whose spiritual dogma masks 'fascist' pol ambitions; group's founder P R Sarkar is in Indian prison awaiting trial on charge of having murdered 6 defectors from cult 2 yrs ago; Anand Marg has conducted internatl campaign charging that Sarkar is being tortured by police; Govt denies these allegations; murder charges and allegations by former members of sadism and homosexuality have thwarted growth of sect in India; sr Anand Marg official estimates that group has 2.5-million members in 37 countries, including 10,000 in US; estimates that nearly 2-million Indians are members, figure that is probably excessive

headline: Homosexual Civil‐Rights Group Is Announced by Ex‐City Aide
abstract: Former NYC Health Services Admr H J Brown, 2 wks after publicly disclosing that he is homosexual, on Oct 15 announces formation of new natl civil rights orgn for homosexual men and women; orgn, called Natl Gay Task Force, is expected to act as clearing house and coordinator for some 850 other homosexual groups in US and to press for Fed legis outlawing discrmination against homosexuals and repealing sodomy laws, among other goals; task force, which lists bd of dirs of 22 homosexual activists, announces it has hired professional staff of 5 and is looking for suitable office space; Brown says force will need annual budget of $150,000 yrly, which he hopes to raise through fund-raising appeals among both homosexuals and non-homosexuals and foundations; Brown illus

headline: Homosexual Teacher Fights to Survive
abstract: Paramus, NJ, hs teacher J N Gish, who informed school bd in '72 that he has been named pres of NJ Gay Activist Alliance, comments on his treatment since that announcement, int; says he has been forbidden to enter school or meet with students, has been cut off from colleagues, had his telephone removed, has been subjected to series of minor harassments and, finally, suspended from his job without pay; discusses question of whether individual can choose his own sexual style without endangering position in classroom; revs bd of educ's attempt to force him to submit to psychiatric examination to determine his fitness to continue as teacher; was granted temporary injunction barring test through efforts of NJ Amer Civil Liberties Union; says bd made issue mental health case while he believes it is civil rights case; parent in dist, Mrs R Armstrong, says she has no objection to his teaching her sons; Gish illus

headline: VICE ISSUE RAISED IN SAN FRANCISCO
abstract: Article on San Francisco's nude encounter parlors in which men can talk about their problems with disrobed woman for $50 an hr; police dept vice squad contends parlors are nothing more than storefront bordellos, or places where men are tricked into thinking they will get sex for money; few arrests have been made for prostitution and solicitation of lewd acts; female parlor employes comment on their activities; city is proposing ordinance that would prohibit women from exposing genitalia or breasts in these situations and prohibit parlors from using words 'nude' or 'naked' in ads; House of Joy operator E Charles says his business does not need prostitution when it nets $5,000 a mo on legitimate basis

headline: MURDER SUSPECT HELD IN 4TH RAPE
abstract: Allweiss charged on Oct 26 by Manhattan Sex and Crimes Squad with 4th rape offense; Judge H Solniker orders that he be sent to Bellevue Hosp for psychiatric examination; at time of his arrest, Allweis was free on $15,000 bail, accused of having raped 3 women on East Side; 4th offense occurred on West Side on Sept 26 and involved sodomy, robbery and burglary; Allweiss's atty says police and Dist Atty's office are guilty of 'breach of faith' because they arrested him 12 hrs before he was to surrender and because they placed him in lineup without his atty present; police say murder motive is other than sex crime

headline: N.B.C. Acts After Complaints By Homosexual Organizations
abstract: NBC officials on Oct 26 acknowledge that TV network has at times dealt unfairly with homosexuals in its programs; agree to maintain continuing liaison with homosexual orgns for advice in future treatment of homosexual topics; agreement was made after meetings at NBC between 4 reprs of Natl Gay Task Force and network execs involved in programming and program standards; meeting was arranged before disruption of Today TV show by M Siegel, later identified as member of Gay Raiders, Phila-based orgn; his intrusion was to have been opening shot of multi-city demonstration against network by Natl Gay Task Force and related homosexual activist orgns; Today show protest was over recent episode of Sanford and Son, which centered on incidents in homosexual bar; Natl Gay Task Force and Gay Activists Alliance have in effect been seeking status as minority group; NBC agreement has been taken as victory by homosexual groups; nationwide demonstrations apparently have not taken place; Task Force communications dir R Gold says he does not know whether any other demonstrations have taken place, but says he is sure 'something was done' in Chicago and Los Angeles

headline: Israel Reports Complete Quiet on Both Fronts for First Time Since War Began
abstract: Israel repts on Oct 27 complete quiet on both Egyptian and Syrian fronts for 1st time since resumption of Middle East hostilities on Oct 6; Israeli mil spokesman says Egyptian 3d Corps remains encircled and isolated on east bank of Suez Canal opposite Suez City; Israel also announces that it has agreed to return 30 severely wounded Egyptian prisoners to Cairo in 1st prisoner release of war; expresses hope that Egypt will reciprocate by exchanging some of most seriously wounded Israeli prisoners; says it has agreed to meeting with Egyptian mil officials to discuss cease-fire as well as transfer of supply convoy to Egyptian 3d Corps; repts that 10 teams of UN observers have taken up positions along cease-fire lines, 7 of which are on Israeli side of Suez front while 3 are stationed near Arab lines; mood among Israeli populace on 1st day of cease-fire is described as subdued, but there reptdly remains tangible tension as nation awaits full accounting of its casualties; toll is said to exceed rept issued 2 wks ago, which listed 656 dead and 2,000 wounded; entrapment of Egyptian 3d Corps by Israeli forces seen posing explosive threat to cease-fire; qualified mil sources estimate that Egyptian units have sufficient water and supplies for 3 to 4 days; Israeli mil spokesman Col N Kharni says there is no sign that Egyptian units are collapsing or ready to retreat; US reptdly has been applying pressure on Israel to relieve plight of 3d Corps for fear that new fighting might erupt as their situation becomes more desperate; peril to maintenance of cease-fire exists on Syrian front, where Arab forces have been resupplying their units with new equipment provided by USSR
